title: Operator experimentation fail-safe patterns and runbook
author: Marisol Ortega
content:
Summary

This document captures operator-focused fail-safe patterns for experimentation on the Redwood platform. It is intended for platform operators, SREs, and feature owners who run experiments (canaries, operator-led A/Bs, kernel or quantization toggles, prefetching experiments) that could affect multitenant inference latency, throughput, or cost. The guidance emphasizes deterministic, low-latency protective actions and a compact runbook operators can follow during a misbehaving experiment.

Scope and goals

- Scope: experimentation that touches runtime routing, batch sizing, kernel selection, tenant prioritization, prefetch hints, or operator-controlled feature flags. Excludes: model training experiments and customer data schema changes.
- Goals: minimize blast radius, enable sub-10 minute full rollback, ensure observable, auditable fail-safe decisions, and preserve tenant SLAs where possible.

When to apply these patterns

Apply these patterns for:
1) Any canary that touches the serving runtime (kernel/precipath).
2) Experiments that change batching, prefetching, or cache eviction heuristics.
3) Operator experiments on tenant slicing, priority credits, or eviction behavior.

Top-level fail-safe primitives (design patterns)

1) Immediate throttling fence (circuit-breaker + soft-quota)
- Mechanism: attach a short-window (30s) error-rate and latency circuit that converts new experimental traffic to a safe baseline (default model variant or existing kernel).
- Thresholds: trip when errors > 5% or 99th-percentile token latency increases > 2x baseline in 30s window.
- Outcome: automatic re-routing to baseline for affected route and a PagerDuty alert.

2) Canary shadowing with active comparison and drift alarm
- Mechanism: fork a copy of production request to the candidate path in shadow mode, compare token latency, token cost, and log-likelihood/quality proxies.
- Drift rule: flag if average per-request divergence metric (configurable similarity score) falls below 0.85 for 5 minutes.

3) Fast rollback toggle (operator-usable feature flag)
- Mechanism: every experiment must include a single CLI/console command that does the rollback; no multi-step manual changes allowed for first-line mitigation.
- Guard rails: the rollback command must be idempotent, emit telemetry, and trigger an SLO impact re-evaluation job.

4) Progressive throttle window (graceful degrade)
- Pattern: instead of full stop, reduce routed qps in a geometric series (75% -> 50% -> 25%) at 90s intervals while monitoring.
- Failure: if metrics continue to degrade after second step, trigger immediate rollback.

5) Quiet-mode operator acknowledgement (human-in-the-loop)
- Use when automated mitigations risk higher customer-impact (e.g., private deployments). Requires a single sign-off on the console and an explicit operator ack window (default 15 minutes). If ack not provided, automated fail-safes run.

Operational runbook (step-by-step)

1) Detect
- Alert sources: canary divergence alarms, token-latency spike, SLO burn > 3% in 5 minutes, abnormal kernel error rates, tenant complaint.
- First action: add "experiment:paused" tag to alert and open an incident channel (#ops-experiments).

2) Triage (2–4 minutes)
- Identify impacted routes and tenants via trace ids and tenant metadata.
- Query the canary dashboard (see Dashboards & Metrics below) and check: 30s error-rate, qps per-route, 99p token latency, cache hit ratio.
- Decide whether to apply automated fence (pattern 1) or move to manual rollback.

3) Immediate containment (under 3 minutes)
- If error-rate > 5% OR 99p latency > 2x: trigger Immediate throttling fence (CLI: redwood experiment fence --id <exp> --action divert).
- If drift score < 0.75 for 5m: trigger rollback command (CLI: redwood experiment rollback --id <exp> --reason="drift").
- Document actions in the incident channel with timestamps and responsible operator.

4) Recover and validate (5–10 minutes)
- Confirm baseline SLOs return to pre-experiment levels (SLO re-evaluation job should complete within 10 minutes).
- Run a lightweight synthetic test harness against the recovered route: 100 requests across representative tenants.
- If recovered, mark experiment as failed and tag for postmortem review.

5) Post-incident actions (within 48 hours)
- Owner runs a short retro: root cause, metric deltas, change to experiment config, and required code changes.
- Update experiment checklist and assign remediation tickets.

Runbook quick commands (examples)

- Divert traffic to baseline:
  redwood experiment fence --id exp-2026-042 --action divert --window 30s

- Full rollback:
  redwood experiment rollback --id exp-2026-042 --reason "latency-regression"

- Force progressive throttle step:
  redwood experiment throttle --id exp-2026-042 --ratio 0.5 --duration 90s

Dashboards & metrics to instrument

Create a compact "experiment health" dashboard per experiment with these panels:
- Canary vs baseline 50th/95th/99th token latency (line chart)
- Token-level cost delta (per-request average token cost)
- Shadow divergence similarity score (0–1) and distribution histogram
- Error-rate (4xx/5xx) and kernel exception types (table)
- Prefetch/caching hit rate and eviction churn (counter)
- Tenant-impact table: top 20 tenants by SLO burn during window

SLO & alert thresholds (recommended defaults)

| Metric | Scope | Alert threshold | Action |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 99p token latency | route-level | > 2x baseline for 30s | auto-fence -> operator page |
| Error rate | route-level | > 5% in 30s | auto-fence -> operator page |
| Shadow divergence | canary-level | < 0.80 for 5m | recommend rollback |
| SLO burn | product-level | > 3% in 5m | immediate incident |
| Cache eviction spike | node/pool | > 200% of baseline rate | investigate prefetch heuristic |
Note: thresholds should be tuned per-runtime and tenant risk class. VIP tenant routes should have lower tolerance (e.g., 1% error-rate threshold).

Ownership and responsibilities

- Experiment owner (feature team): defines success criteria, divergence metric, and preflight checks. Responsible for postmortem.
- Platform operator on-shift: runs runbook, executes containment, and verifies recovery.
- Runtime owners (serving-runtime team): provide fast rollback mechanisms and ensure telemetry hooks.
- Observability team: maintains experiment dashboard templates and alerting rules.

Preflight checklist (required before scheduling any experiment)

1) Automated preflight suite green: integration + 1000 synthetic micro-requests.
2) Has a clearly defined divergence metric and threshold in the experiment spec.
3) Default rollback command validated in staging and smoke-tested in prod-like environment.
4) Dashboard created with required panels and linked to the experiment ticket.
5) Owner identifies blast-radius and lists top-5 impacted tenants.

Safety-by-design examples

- Canary with dual routing: 90% baseline / 10% candidate + 100% shadowing for the first 30 minutes. After stable metrics for 15 minutes, increase candidate percentage in controlled steps.
- Auto-failover variant: deploy candidate as a model variant that can be replaced by a pinned fallback at the load-balancer level in under 30s.

Appendix: operator-oriented snippets and OPA example

Minimal OPA policy fragment to prevent experiments running without rollback command:

```
package experiments

default allow = false

allow {
  input.has_rollback == true
  input.dashboard_link != ""
  input.owner != ""
}
```

Simple JSON experiment spec example:

```
{
  "id": "exp-2026-042",
  "owner": "feature/kv-prefetch",
  "divergence_metric": "cosine_similarity_v2",
  "rollback_cmd": "redwood experiment rollback --id exp-2026-042",
  "traffic_profile": "progressive",
  "max_window_minutes": "120"
}
```
